real_errors.title: The J400 chatter bench rule (< 10 ms per drop-out, < 18 % open in any 100 ms window) is not safe at the worst corner: trains that pass both lines turn a worst-case U9 off at 5.73-6.0 V; 20.0 / 24.4 % is only the fast-chatter (d -> 0) limit
real_errors.evidence: Own model (.supervisor/r25_triage/chatter.py -> chatter.out): EN node with R80 / R165 +1 %, R81 -1 %, C87 0.72 x 220 nF, U9 EN sink 0.1 uA, D402 50 nA (at J400.2 closed, through R165 open), VUVLO(F) 1.116 V (TI SLVSFC9C p9); an exhaustive +/- corner search confirms this is the worst corner. It reproduces the records: single drop-out 6.30 / 8.204 / 10.345 / 20.111 / 26.023 ms at 5.5 / 5.73 / 6.0 / 7.4 / 8.4 V, pack floor for 10 ms 5.96 V, EN 1.4014 V at 6.0 V, averaged trip 20.01 / 24.41 % at 5.73 / 6.0 V. Periodic steady-state trip fraction falls with drop-out length d: 5.73 V 19.9 / 18.9 / 17.7 / 15.1 / 13.6 / 11.8 / 9.6 / 5.8 % at 0.1 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 / 8 ms; 6.0 V 24.3 / 23.4 / 22.3 / 20.0 / 18.6 / 17.2 / 15.6 / 13.7 / 8.3 % at 0.1 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 / 8 / 9.9 ms (reproduces both lenses). Counterexamples that pass < 10 ms and < 18 %: 6.0 V, 8 ms every 50-51 ms (16 %), EN min 1.095-1.098 V; 5.96 V, 8 ms every 57 ms, 1.106 V. A worse class the lenses did not test: clustered drop-outs defeat the per-drop-out rule as well; 3 x 4 ms open with 0.2 ms closures (12 ms in 100 ms = 12 %, longest 4 ms) gives EN 1.028 V at 5.73 V and 1.078 V at 6.0 V; 2 x 5 ms gives 1.073 V at 5.73 V; all trip. So a "longest drop-out" table (REQUIREMENTS-01 option 2) is not conservative either (3 x 4 ms at 12 % passes a 15.1 % line and trips). The C87 = 150 nF functional run (option 3) is not either: a nominal board with 150 nF still tolerates 25.4 / 23.7 / 21.3 % at 0.5 / 2 / 4 ms against the worst-case 19.5 / 17.7 / 15.1 %. The functional "U9 stays on" check screens only the bench board (nominal averaged trip about 26-30 %). A sliding-window total is safe: blocks every 100 ms trip only above 7.63 ms open per 100 ms at 5.73 V (9.59 ms at 6.0 V, 5.87 ms at 5.5 V); a 4000-train adversarial search at 5.73 V under "< 7.62 ms open in any 100 ms window" gave EN min 1.1173 V > 1.116 V (.supervisor/r25_triage/window_rule.py -> window_rule.out).

real_errors.recommended_criterion: Pass line (executable from the contact record the procedure already takes, correct at the worst corner): record the J400 contact state at >= 10 kS/s under flight-level vibration and pass only if the total open time in every sliding 100 ms window is < 7 ms (7.63 ms is the worst-case limit at 5.73 V with C87 220 nF; Calculation), and U9 stays on for the whole run at 5.73 V. This replaces both the < 18 % line and the < 10 ms single-drop-out rule (a single drop-out >= 7 ms already fails it). A switch that fails it may be accepted only if its recorded contact waveform, replayed through the worst-corner EN model above at 5.73 V, keeps EN >= 1.116 V; the periodic trip-fraction table is guidance only. Chosen over the root option (functional run at 5.73 V plus the single-drop-out rule) because the functional run screens only a nominal board and the single-drop-out rule is defeated by clustered drop-outs; over REQUIREMENTS-01 option 2 and 3 for the reasons in the evidence; option 1 (replay) is kept as the less conservative fallback because it needs a committed model script.
real_errors.concrete_fix: Text, records and generated text only. In every place listed in quoted_in: state that 20.0 / 24.4 % is the d -> 0 limit; replace "< 10 ms" and "< 18 %" by the window rule above (< 7 ms open in any 100 ms window at 5.73 V, U9 stays on; optional worst-corner replay); give the d-dependent trip fractions as guidance; correct "drop-outs shorter than ... cannot trip U9" to "a single drop-out shorter than ...". Edit the chatter obligation in m3_design/r10_sch_check.py line 295, regenerate r10_binding_note.json (K-binding) and update the words pinned in tools/test_r10_check.py. Record a new decision (D-R25-NN). Raising C87 (BOM only, same land) remains the owner alternative if a real switch cannot meet 7 ms.

real_errors.title: U9's OVLO corner 9.97 V is called "the highest RAW_PROTECTED can reach" but omits the OVLO pin leakage (IOVLKG +/-0.1 uA); with it the highest trip is 10.18 V
real_errors.evidence: TI SLVSFC9C section 6.5 (cached tps25947.pdf, OVLO block): VOV(R) 1.183-1.223 V, IOVLKG -0.1 to 0.1 uA at 0.5-1.5 V. Board BOM: R82 2M 0.1 % (C4241878), R83 280k 0.1 % (C705755). Trip = (VOV(R) + I x R82||R83) x (R82+R83)/R83 at the 0.1 % corners: 9.4163-10.1764 V with leakage, 9.6161-9.9762 V without. Consequences: buck prospective all-shorts peak 3.645 / 3.616 -> about 3.657 / 3.627 A (470 / 500 kHz; recomputed with the generator's peak() formula); U9 port-fault bound 3.74380 -> about 3.74386 A, still below U9's 3.946 A minimum limit, so r10_parts.py's assert holds.
